name: Useful Edges
description: You are given a weighted undirected graph on $$$n$$$ vertices along with $$$q$$$ triples $$$(u, v, l)$$$, where in each triple $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ are vertices and $$$l$$$ is a positive integer. An edge $$$e$$$ is called useful if there is at least one triple $$$(u, v, l)$$$ and a path (not necessarily simple) with the following properties: $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ are the endpoints of this path, $$$e$$$ is one of the edges of this path, the sum of weights of all edges on this path doesn't exceed $$$l$$$. Please print the number of useful edges in this graph.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2\leq n\leq 600$$$, $$$0\leq m\leq \frac{n(n-1)}2$$$). Each of the following $$$m$$$ lines contains three integers $$$u$$$, $$$v$$$ and $$$w$$$ ($$$1\leq u, v\leq n$$$, $$$u\neq v$$$, $$$1\leq w\leq 10^9$$$), denoting an edge connecting vertices $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ and having a weight $$$w$$$. The following line contains the only integer $$$q$$$ ($$$1\leq q\leq \frac{n(n-1)}2$$$) denoting the number of triples. Each of the following $$$q$$$ lines contains three integers $$$u$$$, $$$v$$$ and $$$l$$$ ($$$1\leq u, v\leq n$$$, $$$u\neq v$$$, $$$1\leq l\leq 10^9$$$) denoting a triple $$$(u, v, l)$$$. It's guaranteed that: the graph doesn't contain loops or multiple edges; all pairs $$$(u, v)$$$ in the triples are also different.
output_specification: Print a single integer denoting the number of useful edges in the graph.
approach_summary: Compute all-pairs shortest paths or reachability using triple loop dynamic programming d[i][j] = min(d[i][j], d[i][k] + d[k][j]) in O(V^3) time.
